recipes.name: Mashed Sweet Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 6 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
0.75 cup warm 2% milk, or as needed
0.75 cup maple syrup, or to taste
0.5 cup softened butter, cut into chunks

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add sweet potatoes, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer until tender, 20 to 30 minutes. Drain and transfer sweet potatoes to a large bowl.
Mash sweet potatoes with a potato masher until mostly smooth.
Gradually stir in milk until sweet potatoes reach desired consistency.
Stir in syrup and butter until smooth.

raw_recipe.headline: Mashed Sweet Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: This mashed sweet potatoes recipe makes smooth mashed sweet potatoes enriched with butter, warm milk, and maple syrup; the perfect savory-sweet side.

video.description: Mashed sweet potatoes are flavored with maple syrup and butter.

review.reviewBody: I didn't have maple syrup in the house so I replaced the maple syrup with 1/4 cup of brown sugar and 1/2 cup of honey...boy did I get rave reviews from the family! Everyone loved this, including my youngest daughter who can be quite picky when it comes to vegetables. This will be seen on our dinner table again!

"6 potatoes" doesn't mean anything given the large size range in even a single bag. I used 8 small to medium potatoes, which came out to just under 2 lbs before peeling. Next time say "2 lbs" or "3 lbs" or whatever quantity matches the rest of the ingredients.

With the 2 lbs of potatoes I used half the recommended butter (half a stick = 1/4 cup), 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup milk, and no syrup. I also added 1/2 tsp sea salt because any recipe with sugar is cloying without it, and 1/2 tsp vanilla.

Sweet potatoes are always stringy when thrown directly into a mixer, so I squeezed them through a potato ricer directly into the mixing bowl and stirred with a spoon. An unexpected benefit is that boiled potatoes absorb a lot of water, and using the ricer squeezed out some of the excess liquid into the sink before the potatoes started coming through. The result was still slightly loose, so next time I'll try leaving out the milk altogether. But the flavor and the stringless texture were perfect.

My family LOVED these, and requested a repeat soon..... especially my teenage boys! If I could take away half a star I would, only because I made the recipe with several spices (not included in the original), and otherwise used HockeyMom's tweaks. The idea, however, is super-simple and easy to make! How I made it: I used approx. 3 lbs. of sweet potatoes (they come in such varied sizes, it's hard to know what "6" means). After draining the potatoes, I simply used a hand masher right in the pot.... no need to dirty anything else. I melted in 4 tbsp. butter, then mixed it with 1/3 cup of milk, slightly more than 1/3 cup of real maple syrup, and spices: 1/8 tsp. nutmeg, 1/8 tsp. cloves, and 1 tsp. cinnamon. This makes good portions for a family of 5-6. Delicious!!

Very nice recipe. It was a bit sweet so I only added 2 tablespoons of brown sugar instead of the syrup. A mixer eliminates the strings in the potatoes (they wrap around the blades) and makes them so much smoother, but the recipe is great either way.

Subbed cream for 1/2 the milk. Also added about 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon. Instead of maple syrup I used a bit of molasses (maybe 2 teaspoons tops) , honey (same), and brown sugar (1 tbsp). By being careful to not use too much of those “sweeteners”, I wound up with a nice side dish that didn’t have that holiday “sticky sweet” quality. Served it alongside honey/soy marinated baked chicken thighs. Perfect.

My family likes sweet.potatoes with heat! I peeled & cut up 2 large sweet potatoes. After I boiled & drained them I put them back in the same pot. I mashed them with a potato masher. I added butter then cinnamon, salt, pepper, ground red pepper flake. When I reheat them at dinner time I will add a little brown sugar.

I liked the recipe because of its simplicity. I did modify it because I didn’t want to use syrup and I wanted pecans. MODIFICATIONS: after boiling and draining sweet potatoes, I put them in an oven safe pie glass dish, hand mashed, added the buttter, brown sugar (start with half of a 1/4 cup and continue to add based on how sweet you want them), added milk and mashed it and mixed it altogether in the glass pie baking dish. When I was happy with the flavor, I smoothed the top so it looked ‘pretty’. Then I added whole pecans for decoration and then crumbled fresh pecans and sprinkled them on top. Then I drizzled honey over the pecans and baked for approximately 20-30 minutes. I will try to add a picture - not only was it incredibly delicious (even my sweet potatoes ‘haters’ devoured it!) It so easy to make!

I really enjoyed these sweet potatoes! I drained the potatoes and added the butter first. Then I slowly added the milk until I liked the consistency. It was less than called for. Then I added the maple syrup, a little at a time, until I liked the sweetness. Again, a little less than called for. This is an easy recipe to make to suit one’s own preferences.

Very simple recipe. Here some details how I did it to clarify the proportions: 4 pounds of sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 inch slices. Boiled for about 15 min, then drained and mashed with 1 stick of cold butter (4 ounces), 6 ounces of warm milk, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Added 1.5 tablspoons of brown sugar, which was a little too much, but still tasted good. Next time I would add 1 teaspoon at a time, until you can taste the flavor. This amount was more than sufficient for a group of 20 people, as one of many side dishes. If you make this instead of regular mashed potatoes, the above would probably only serve 10-12 people.

Loved it. I knew that the ingredient quantities showing meant this recipe would be super sweet - so I cut in half all the ingredients (except the potatoes, of course). As I was stirring the potato mix, I sprinkled about a half teaspoon of cinnamon into the mix. It came out perfect - but still wonderfully sweet. I will definitely make this again multiple times. 5 STARS !!!

Yummy! I used twice the sweet potatoes and 3/4 cup half and half along with the 3/4 cup maple syrup. I also added a teaspoon of vanilla extract and 1/3 brown sugar to the boiling water. This should be a dessert it’s so good!!

I love sweet potato and this recipe is awesome! I replace honey for maple syrup from the recipe tip and it is sweet enough to me, I can eat this for breakfast and add some fruit and granola as a leftover! or eggs to fill me up when I don't have time to cook to go to the program or want to go out in early morning.
Delicious! I made with sugar-free almond milk and sprinkled some sage on top. Yum.
Really nice flavor. Perfect side! Not overly sweet.
Used 1/2 the amount of butter. Husband loves to eat the leftovers cold for a nighttime snack.
My whole family LOVED it! Will definitely be making these often. Made it exactly as written
Subs the milk with heavy cream and the syrup with honey , 3 potatoes , delicious and could have used about 4-5potatoes skin on

Excellent recipe. My girlfriend and I made it exactly as the directions stated. I loved that it says to pour the milk in slowly until desired texture because you likeky won't need all of it depending on the size of the sweet potatoes. Make sure to use real maple syrup. I will be making this one again. Thanks

I love to make these with less butter and less maple syrup.. It’s easy to taste test as you make it by using half of each ingredient after the potatoes are mashed. I put the butter in first so it melts and I’ve used vanilla almond milk successfully. I also add a little vanilla and crushed pecans. It’s easy to make these as a good calorie conscientious side dish by cutting way back on butter and maple syrup . I live alone so I eat it hot after making it and then fill several small airtight containers. I love to eat cold as a snack. Mine has lasted for a couple weeks in the fridge.

Ingredients were good but someone else was correct in saying the potatoes need to be listed in recipe by weight. Too runny. And sweet potatoes do not absorb milk like regular potatoes do. Would make again but use my own judgement for the butter, milk and syrup.
